```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, comment = NA)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")

bayesplot::bayesplot_theme_set(ggplot2::theme_gray())
bayesplot::color_scheme_set(scheme = "brightblue")
```

In this vignette, we use the template model "ex-augm-onset-single-intro" where surveys are conditioned on single introduction and follow the times of onset.
For simplicity the model assumes no asymptomatic cases.
This time we load the parameter definitions directly from the model template.

```{r}
hhsimul <- housepi::HouseholdModel$new("augm-onset-single-intro")

# use example parameters associated to the template model
hhsimul$load_param_template()

# inspect parameter definitions used for simulations
hhsimul$param_defs
```

## Infectivity Profile

In `housepi` we follow the convention for infectivity profiles to be function of the generation time.
Generation time is defined as the time from infection to transmission.

Certain profiles will then be conditioned on individual incubation period $\tau$ as follows.

| Time                       | Infector Condition    | Infectee Condition    |
|----------------------------|-----------------------|-----------------------|
| generation                 | \-                    | \-                    |
| from onset to transmission | $\tau_{\rm infector}$ | \-                    |
| serial                     | $\tau_{\rm infector}$ | $\tau_{\rm infectee}$ |

We can provide a custom infectivity proifle with the method `$add_infec_profile()`.
At any moment, we can showcase the loaded profile as follows:

```{r, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=3, fig.fullwidth=TRUE, out.height="auto", fig.align="center"}
# we associate a gamma for infectivity profile
hhsimul$add_infec_profile(name = "gamma",
                          args = c(shape = 2.2, scale = 1.3))

# extract profile and other general information
infec <- hhsimul$showcase_infec_profile()

# plot instantaneous and cumulative profile with ggplot2
library(ggplot2)

# format title with information from the export
title <- sprintf("Infectivity Profile: %s [mean=%.1f, sd=%.1f]",
                 stringr::str_to_title(infec$name),
                 infec$mean, sqrt(infec$var))

# coefficient to rescale cumulative
rescale <- max(infec$profile$cumul) / max(infec$profile$inst)

ggplot(infec$profile, aes(x = gentime)) +
  # plot cumulative profile
  theme(axis.ticks.y.right = element_line(color = "coral"),
        axis.text.y.right = element_text(color = "coral"),
        axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = "coral")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = cumul / rescale), color = "coral") +
  # plot instantaneous
  geom_line(aes(y = inst)) +
  # apply rescaling
  scale_y_continuous(name = "Instantaneous",
                     sec.axis = sec_axis(~. * rescale, name = "Cumulative")) +
  labs(x = "Generation Time", title = title)
```

Bear in mind that each model requiring an infectivity profile has a default profile.
For more details on how to customize infectivity profiles, check the vignette [Customize Models](customize_models.html).

## Simulate an Outbreak

We propose the following definitions for the augmented variable.

```{r}
# associate defininitions from a list
hhsimul$load_augm_list(
  
  # define 'infec_time' as the difference between onset and incubation
  infec_time = "onset_time@A - incub_period@A",
  
  # define an 'onset_time' for each individual
  onset_time = list(
    init_rand = TRUE,
    model = "lnorm",
    args = c(meanlog = 4, sdlog = 0.5),
    max = 365
  ),
  # define an 'incub_period' for each individual
  incub_period = list(
    init_rand = TRUE,
    model = "gamma",
    # assign arguments of incubation period from parameter definitions
    args = c(shape = "inc_shape",  scale = "inc_scale"),
    max = 14
  ),
  # add infection time definition
  infec_time = "onset_time@A - incub_period@A"
)

# append incubation period distribution parameters as constants
hhsimul$load_param_list(inc_shape = 2, inc_scale = 1.1, append = TRUE)
```

We then run a simulation with the method `simulate`.

```{r}
# simulate using the data structure from the survey
data("survey", package = "housepi")
survey$status <- NA
simulated <- hhsimul$simulate(survey, seed = 3413)

# in addition to final status, we associated  augmented variables
# incubation period onset time
head(simulated)

# assume onsets after 6 PM are reported to next day
is_infec <- simulated$status == 1
simulated$onset_date <- NA
simulated[is_infec, "onset_date"] <- sapply(
  simulated[is_infec, "onset_time"],
  # simulation onset date > 18/24
  function(x) floor(ifelse((x %% 1) > 0.75, x + 1, x))
)

# remove onobserved quantities simulated dataset
simulated$incub_period <- NULL
simulated$onset_time <- NULL
simulated$infec_time <- NULL

head(simulated)
```

## Validate the Simulation

We can check that inference returns the parameters used for the simulation.

```{r}
# make a deep clone of simulation object to re-use previous definitions
hhmodel <- hhsimul$clone(deep = FALSE)

# load definitions from list (automatically drop previous definitions)
hhmodel$load_augm_list(
  infec_time = "onset_time@A - incub_period@A",
  
  onset_time = list(
    value = "onset_date@D",
    rule = "norm", scale = 0.25, from = "onset_date@D"
  ),
  
  incub_period = list(
    init_rand = TRUE,
    model = "gamma", args = c(shape = "inc_shape", scale = "inc_scale"),
    max = 14, rule = "draw"
  )
)

# perform the inference
# note: NA onset dates of healthy individuals will raise a warning
hhmodel$infer(simulated, n_chains = 3,
              n_adapt = 2000, n_steps = 10000,
              n_burnin = 1000, thin = 10,
              seed = 3731, progress = 30)
```

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=4, fig.fullwidth=TRUE, out.height="auto", fig.align="center"}
# use bayesplot to plot the traces
library(bayesplot)
mcmc_trace(hhmodel$traces)
```

```{r, fig.width=5, fig.height=2.5, fig.fullwidth=TRUE, out.height="auto", fig.align="center"}
# extract the traces without loglikelihood
trs <- hhmodel$traces_no_loglike

# compute Rhat values associate to inferred parameters
array_mcmc <- simplify2array(lapply(trs, as.matrix))
rhat <- apply(array_mcmc, ifelse(is.list(trs), 2, 3), rstan::Rhat)

# use bayesplot to showcase Rhat statistics
mcmc_rhat(rhat) +
  yaxis_text(hjust = 1)
```

Here we performed R-hat diagnostics computing the values of $\hat{R}$ with [rstan](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rstan/).

Finally we wrap all together to compare to parameters used for simulation.

```{r}
# collect the results
results <- hhmodel$traces_results

# compare results to parameter values used for simulation
simul_param_defs <- hhsimul$param_defs
imask <- simul_param_defs$const == FALSE
inames <- simul_param_defs[imask, ]$name
```

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,}
library(dplyr)
library(flextable)
cbind(Simulated = simul_param_defs[imask, ]$value, results) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("Parameter") |>
  mutate(Inferred = sprintf("%0.4f [%0.4f, %0.4f]",
                            mean, cri_lower, cri_upper)) |>
  select(-mean, -sd, -cri_lower, -cri_upper) |>
  flextable() |>
  separate_header() |>
  theme_vanilla() |>
  bold(j = ~ Parameter, bold = TRUE) |>
  autofit()
```

### Model Comparison

We can estimate the model "evidence" (also known as "marginal loglikelihood") with the method of the power posteriors:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# return the estimate of the model evidence
evidence <- hhmodel$evidence(n_rungs = 30, n_burnin = 500, n_steps = 5000)

ggplot(evidence$detail, aes(x = inv_temper, y = mean_loglike)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = "Inverse Temperature", y = "Mean Loglikelihood")

evidence$estimate
```
